Subject: FinTrust — Processing geography, subprocessors, and deletion flows (Q&A)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. A few quick questions from our security and procurement teams as we evaluate Redwood for Prod ingestion:

- In which countries/regions do you process customer request payloads (inference requests, embeddings, and logs) for hosted customers? For Dedicated/Private what differs?
- Which subprocessors are involved (compute, storage, monitoring, analytics)? Please include vendor names and the regions they operate in.
- Do you perform any cross-border transfers of customer data (including cached/auxiliary artifacts)? If so, what legal mechanisms and safeguards do you use?
- What is your deletion workflow and SLAs? If a customer requests deletion, how long until cached KV, model context, and logs are gone?

Could you attach a current data flow diagram and a subprocessor inventory we can share with our GRC team? Also, we will need SOC 2 Type II or an attestation to move forward.

Appreciate the help — copying our security alias for visibility (security.ops@fintrust.com).

—Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I summarized answers below and attached our latest artefacts (data_flow_map_v2.pdf, subprocessor_inventory.csv). Please let me know if you want a short walkthrough call with Rishi (our infra lead).

High-level:
- Hosted accounts: request handling and short-lived KV/cache operate in one of our regional clusters based on account enrollment (US: us-east-1, EU: eu-west-1 (Ireland), APAC: asia-southeast1 Singapore). Persistent storage for logs/metrics is retained in the same region when possible; some analytics/backup replicas may be stored in the US for operational reasons.
- Dedicated / Private: customers can pin processing to a single region or self-host (VPC/on-prem); in those modes no cross-border transfers occur unless the customer opts in to multi-region failover.
- Subprocessors (examples in attached inventory): compute (AWS EC2/EKS - us-east-1, eu-west-1), object storage (AWS S3 - us-east-1, eu-west-1), metrics/logging (LogStream Inc. - us-east-1), identity/KMS partners (KeySafe Ltd. - hosted KMS in eu-west-1), and CDN/caching partners. The CSV includes contact and region columns.
- Cross-border transfers: for hosted customers we may route ephemeral inference traffic between regions for failover or capacity (e.g., a short-lived fallback to US if EU capacity is exhausted). Transfers are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+/mTLS for internal APIs) and at rest (AES-256). We rely on contractual controls (our DPA includes SCCs where applicable) and operational isolation. For Dedicated/Private customers we can commit to region-local processing in the contract.
- Deletion workflow & SLAs:
  - KV/prefix caches: removed within 30 minutes of the deletion request; eviction + background purge completes within 24 hours for active caches.
  - Inference context (runtime tokens/KV): cleared immediately from the serving runtime on request; any persisted checkpoints are expunged within 7 days.
  - Logs/metrics: customer-identifiable logs are redacted and retained for up to 90 days by default; we offer shorter retention (30/14/7 days) as a configurable setting for enterprise contracts.

Attachments: data_flow_map_v2.pdf (diagram), subprocessor_inventory.csv (vendor, region, contract owner).

Next steps: Rishi — can you confirm the KMS/backups residency and the exact wording we should provide to procurement around SCCs/DPA?

Best,
Olga

Hi all — adding a few technical clarifications and the procurement-safe phrasing below:

1) KMS & backups:
- Customer-managed KMS: supported for Dedicated and Private deployments (bring-your-own-key). For hosted accounts we use KeySafe Ltd. (eu-west-1 for EU accounts) for envelope encryption; master keys are rotated quarterly and access is logged.
- Backups: persistent snapshots are encrypted and stored in the same region where feasible; disaster recovery replicas may be located in a secondary region (listed in the CSV). Replicas are covered by our encryption and contractual controls.

2) Subprocessor specifics (short list):
- AWS (compute & object storage): us-east-1 (primary), eu-west-1 (EU), asia-southeast1 (APAC)
- Google Cloud (optional analytics pipelines): europe-west1
- LogStream Inc. (operational logs aggregation): us-east-1
- DataTransit Inc. (edge routing / burst egress): eu-west-1, us-east-1
(Full inventory attached in the CSV entry with SOC/compliance columns.)

3) Cross-border transfers & legal safeguards:
- For EU-to-US transfers (hosted accounts), we contractually rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) embedded in our DPA and additional technical controls (encryption at rest + strict access controls).
- For customers needing no transfers, we offer Dedicated/Private where we contractually restrict processing to the customer's chosen region and include auditability clauses.

4) Deletion and verification: what we provide in enterprise contracts/procurement: 
- SLA: deletion propagation confirmation within 72 hours for all persisted artifacts; immediate runtime eviction is guaranteed.
- Evidence: a signed deletion certificate (PDF) and an execution log snippet (timestamped) on request; for high-sensitivity customers we can add automated webhook callbacks confirming deletion events.

5) SOC 2 / attestations:
- We maintain SOC 2 Type II — we can provide a redacted report under NDA and include an ISAE/SOC attestation URL for procurement.

Procurement-friendly wording you can paste into an SOW/DPA: "Redwood Inference will process customer data in the geographic region selected by the customer for Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted deployments, Redwood will process data in regional clusters; limited cross-border transfers for failover and operational continuity may occur, governed by the DPA (including SCCs) and supported by industry-standard encryption. Redwood will honor deletion requests per the agreed SLA and provide verifiable deletion evidence upon request."

If you want, I can join a 30-minute call with FinTrust procurement Monday to walk through the CSV and SOC access.

—Rishi
